text: For a differentiable f: ℝⁿ → ℝ, the directional derivative D_v f(p) in the direction of a unit vector v equals:
choices: the Jacobian matrix of f evaluated at p
∇f(p) · v, the dot product of the gradient with v
explanation: The book's theorem gives D_v f(p) = ∇f(p) · v = Df(p)(v): the directional derivative is a scalar obtained by dotting the gradient with the direction. The gradient ∇f is an entire vector, not this scalar, and its magnitude |∇f| is only the maximal directional derivative, attained when v points along ∇f. The distinction between the gradient and the directional derivative is the point being tested.
